precepts.text: But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses. That is the history it goes back to.
precepts.point: When Deacon mentioned the circumcision, that goes back to the history in Acts chapter 15, meaning the Pharisees were pushing first and foremost that they had to circumcise after the manner of Moses, meaning the old covenant of animal sacrifice, and not Christ. So not just circumcision meaning your foreskin, because that is a law that we have to do, but they pushed that before they pushed Christ.

note.label: Lucifer: The Antichrist

precepts.why:
John is the only one in the Bible who calls a system or a person the antichrist. The prophets spoke of that last kingdom that would fight against Christ at his return, but they did not call it antichrist. John says “as ye have heard that antichrist shall come”, which is future, “even now are there many antichrists”. Anti means against. Even in John's time many were against Christ.

“They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us”. These were men among the apostles who up and left the apostles and their teachings, which were the teachings of Christ, and went out teaching against them. They said the resurrection had taken place already. They taught that you have to be circumcised. That is an antichrist doctrine, one form of antichrist in the time of the apostles.

That goes back to the history in Acts 15: “But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.” The Pharisees were pushing first and foremost that they had to be circumcised after the manner of Moses, meaning the old covenant of animal sacrifice, and not Christ. It is not only circumcision of the foreskin, because that is a law we have to do; it is that they pushed that before they pushed Christ.

So from the beginning there were many antichrists: those who went out from the apostles and taught contrary to Christ. That is why John says “they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us.”

precepts.text: And to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written. As it is written. Meaning they had to go back and search. Wait, this was written here. So it makes sense what happened in this particular place of the book, because the prophets wrote about it. That is precept upon precept. Not Hebrew hopscotch. That is understanding the history.
precepts.point: As it is also written. As it is written.

note.label: Give Diligence

precepts.why:
Paul declares that God “hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee.” As it is also written. Acts 15 says the same thing when the apostles came together: “And to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written”.

As it is written means they had to go back and search: wait, this was written here. What happened in that particular place of the book makes sense because the prophets wrote about it. The glad tidings Paul preached were not something new; they were the promise made unto the fathers, fulfilled unto their children, and the prophets had already written it.

That is precept upon precept. Christians call it Hebrew hopscotch and cherry-picking, but it is studying and understanding the word of God, understanding the history and what things must take place. The apostles themselves did it: they took what was happening and laid it beside what the prophets wrote.

Those who do not have the spirit of the Lord cannot do it, and they want to shame us for having understanding and being able to go from Genesis to Revelation and give the understanding thereof. We are going to keep on going precept upon precept, confounding you negroes, because that is how the apostles taught: as it is written.

precepts.text: At the end of Acts 15, Paul and Barnabas had a dispute, and that is who they had the dispute over: John Mark. Barnabas stuck up for him because it was his nephew. It shows you not just anybody can travel. Paul gave him a chance, and when it came to the work he was nowhere to be found. Paul said he is not coming with me any more; Barnabas said, that is my sister's son, I am taking him with me. And the contention was so sharp between them that they departed asunder one from the other.
precepts.point: Epaphras was a self-starter. He did not need someone right there to get the ground running. He heard the truth, believed it, and went and taught it.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
“And Barnabas determined to take with them John, whose surname was Mark. But Paul thought not good to take him with them, who departed from them from Pamphylia, and went not with them to the work.” That is the Marcus of Colossians 4:10, Barnabas’ sister’s son.

“And the contention was so sharp between them, that they departed asunder one from the other: and so Barnabas took Mark, and sailed unto Cyprus; And Paul chose Silas, and departed, being recommended by the brethren unto the grace of God. And he went through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the churches.”

It shows you not just anybody can travel. Paul gave him a chance, and when it came to the work he was nowhere to be found; he came up missing. Paul said straight, I do not care if that is your nephew, he is not traveling with me any more. Barnabas said, that is my sister’s son, I am taking him with me. You can understand that dynamic. The faithful ministers like Epaphras are the ones who stay with the work.

precepts.text: Certain men from Judaea taught the brethren, except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved. Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, and went up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question, declaring the conversion of the Gentiles, the diaspora. But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying that it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses: not only circumcision, but back to animal sacrifice. This is intruding into those things not seen, vainly puffed up: the bright idea that they had to do all those sacrifices of Numbers 28 or they could not be saved. Is that what Christ told the apostles?
precepts.point: How do you go about not being beguiled? If you study, you do not willingly give yourself over to men that will deceive you by handling the word of God deceitfully. Study to shew thyself approved, that you will be able to withstand these men.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
“intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind,” “And not holding the Head”. Who's the head? Christ. What were they intruding into? Acts 15 is an example.

“And certain men which came down from Judea taught the brethren, and said, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.” If you ain't circumcised, you don't get salvation. “When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas, and certain other of them, should go up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question.”

They passed through Phenice and Samaria, “declaring the conversion of the Gentiles”, the diaspora, “and they caused great joy unto all the brethren.” At Jerusalem “they declared all things that God had done with them.”

Then here it comes: “But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.” Which believed: they said they accepted Christ. But they wanted them to go back to the animal sacrifice, not only get circumcised.

That is the bright idea. These negros have bright ideas: reading the scriptures on their own, the light bulb over the head, telling people they don't need nobody. They looked in the scriptures and said you got to do all those sacrifices of Numbers 28 or else you can't be saved. Is that what Christ told the apostles? That is intruding into those things not seen, vainly puffed up by a fleshly mind, and not holding the Head.

precepts.text: Certain which went out from us have troubled you with words, subverting your souls, saying, ye must be circumcised, and keep the law: to whom we gave no such commandment. The apostles said that order did not come from us. It seemed good to send chosen men with our beloved Barnabas and Paul, men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
precepts.point: How do you go about not being beguiled? If you study, you do not willingly give yourself over to men that will deceive you by handling the word of God deceitfully. Study to shew thyself approved, that you will be able to withstand these men.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
The apostles answered those Pharisees: “Forasmuch as we have heard, that certain which went out from us have troubled you with words, subverting your souls, saying, Ye must be circumcised, and keep the law”. Troubled you with words, subverting your souls: getting you away from Christ. Keep the law here is the law of animal sacrifice.

“to whom we gave no such commandment”. Hear what the apostles said: we didn't give that order; that didn't come from us. “It seemed good unto us, being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men unto you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,” “Men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.”

So you see the problem. Christ was dealing with the apostles, and Christ never told the apostles they had to get circumcised and deal with animal sacrifice. But these Pharisees that believed looked in the scriptures and put their bright ideas to them.

That is “vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind” in Colossians 2:18: I'm the priest, I understand it, not you apostles. And it is “not holding the Head”. The men who came from Judea went out from the apostles without their commandment, and the believers were beguiled by words the apostles never gave.

precepts.text: To this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written, after this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down. What does that mean? Bring back the twelve tribes: the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom. When God accepted Cornelius and his kinsmen, James quoted this.
precepts.point: Cornelius was a centurion of the Italian band, a devout man that feared God with all his house. Where was he from? Caesarea. On the map, Caesarea sits right above Samaria: that's Manasseh's land. Cornelius was northern kingdom, not a Gentile of the nations. Do some research; do some study.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
When God accepted Cornelius and his kinsmen in Acts 10, the apostles came together in Acts 15, and James said, “to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written, After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down”.

What does that mean? Bring back the twelve tribes of Israel. Bring back the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom. Christians do not realize it; ask them what happened to the northern kingdom and they say, I don’t know.

“And I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up: That the residue of men might seek after the Lord”: they are going to seek him in slavery. “And all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called”: those that call themselves Jewish and those that call themselves Christian.

So the accepting of Cornelius was the beginning of that building again. The tabernacle of David fell when the kingdom split, and bringing Cornelius, a northern kingdom man out of Manasseh’s land, into the fold is God starting to put the two kingdoms back together.

precepts.text: Assembled with one accord, they sent chosen men, Barnabas and Paul, men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Bishops, deacons, and captains on one accord send chosen men who risk their lives in the hoods of Haiti, Africa, and Puerto Rico. Michael Jordan is not risking anything. And leaders build leaders: a father wants his son to be better than him, and a leader whose mindset is job security in the high seat will be removed.
precepts.point: Public service announcement: IUIC is not a fractured organization; with the Most High we are thriving. Passover season is coming and the tree gets shaken, so do not fall out of it over Easter with your mother's white dress and tall hat.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
Mattathias would not do what everybody else was doing. He cried, “Whosoever is zealous of the law, and maintaineth the covenant, let him follow me.” Somebody had to stand up, and that is the mark of a true leader. Acts shows what the leaders of the church were doing: “It seemed good unto us, being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men unto you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul, Men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.”

Assembled with one accord: bishops on one accord, deacons on one accord, captains on one accord. And they send chosen men, not just anybody. You could say they send out Bishop Nathanyel and Deacon Isaac, as they sent Barnabas and Paul.

“Men that have hazarded their lives”: a real leader risks his life for Christ. They call Michael Jordan a leader, football coaches leaders of men; Michael Jordan is not risking anything. Wyclef, what are you doing? The men of this camp have been to Haiti, to Africa, to the barrios of Puerto Rico. They are not going to the suburbs; they are going to the hood, all over IUIC, putting their lives on the line for the name of Christ.

And leaders build leaders. That is an attribute of a father: a father wants his son to be better than him. The bishops are building leadership, sending men to countries and corners that could not be touched before, and now others have been raised up to touch them. But if your mindset is job security, sitting in the high seat, and not building brothers to be better than yourself, forget about it: the Lord will remove you.

precepts.text: Certain men which came down from Judaea taught the brethren, except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved; after the manner of Moses, sacrifice followed circumcision on the eighth day. Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension with them and went up to Jerusalem, where there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying it was needful to circumcise them and command them to keep the law of Moses. These are the false brethren brought in unawares that Galatians addresses.
precepts.point: Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years; I am afraid of you, lest I have bestowed upon you labour in vain. Colossians 2:16: let no man judge you in meat or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days, which are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ. Ezekiel 45:17 answers both: it was the prince's part to give burnt offerings, meat offerings, and drink offerings in the feasts, the new moons, the sabbaths, and all solemnities, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel. On each of those days you had to sacrifice, and the Pharisees, whose bread and butter was people bringing animals, were trying to win the churches back to temple law, saying to hell with what Christ did. If you need an animal, you are condemned, because the temple would be destroyed.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
Who was bewitching the Galatians back into bondage? “And certain men which came down from Judea taught the brethren, and said, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.” After the manner of Moses, sacrifice followed circumcision, on the eighth day. To be circumcised after the manner of Moses meant going back to sacrifice.

“When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas, and certain other of them, should go up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question.” These men came from Judea infiltrating and causing confusion, saying you have to sacrifice.

“But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.” The Pharisees came in as believers, part of the church, and were imposing that you had to sacrifice according to the manner of Moses. These are the same false brethren brought in unawares that Galatians addresses, who came in privily to spy out our liberty and bring us into bondage.

As the movement grew, the Pharisees went into the churches to win them back to temple law. Paul said he profited in the Jews' religion; people bringing animals was their bread and butter. They were saying to hell with what Christ did, you need an animal for atonement. Paul's answer: if you do, you are condemned, because the temple would be destroyed.

precepts.text: Simeon hath declared how God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name, Acts 10, and to this agree the words of the prophets: after this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down, and I will build again the ruins thereof, and set it up. Build again is the reconciliation and the reparation of all twelve tribes. Then verse 17: that the residue of men, the rest of the nations, might seek after the Lord, and all the Gentiles upon whom my name is called, the Christians, who try to include themselves in our restoration and adoption.
precepts.point: Sin is the transgression of the law, 1 John 3:4. Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law: those under the law break it and are under sin, and both Jews and Gentiles under sin means both under the law, which the other nations never were. That every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God, the world that received God's commandments under Moses. Therefore by the deeds of the law, sacrifice, there shall no flesh be justified in his sight, for we are justified by Christ's blood; for by the law is the knowledge of sin, because to acknowledge a sin, willful or ignorant, you had to bring an animal.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
Paul says “we have before proved both Jews and Gentiles, that they are all under sin”, and the Gentiles there are Israelites. Acts 15 shows the same Gentiles being restored: “Simeon hath declared how God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name.” That references what took place in Acts 10, and we understand that is talking about Israel.

“And to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written, After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down; and I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up”. Build again: that is the reconciliation, that is the reparation. It had fallen down because we became filthy, and God restores the waste places. Who is that? All twelve tribes of Israel.

Then verse 17: “That the residue of men might seek after the Lord”. The residue is the rest of the nations outside of the twelve tribes: Edom and the others. “And all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called”: that is the Christians, and the Jews.

They try to include themselves in our reconciliation, our restoration and our adoption. But the building again is of David’s tabernacle, the twelve tribes; the residue only seeks after the Lord once Israel is set up again.

precepts.text: In that day God raises up the tabernacle of David that is fallen.
precepts.point: The residue of men seek after the Lord in servitude, and the Gentiles called by his name are those who call themselves Jews and Christians.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
Isaiah spoke of “the day that the Lord bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.” What does it mean to bind up the breach of his people? Acts 15 answers it. “Simeon hath declared how God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name. And to this agree the words of the prophets”: “After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down”. That is bringing back the twelve tribes of Israel.

James was quoting Amos: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof”. Closing up the breaches is the binding up of the breach in Isaiah 30: when he gathers the twelve tribes of Israel back again. Right now the tabernacle is still fallen; we are trying to gather ourselves together. “and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old”.

“That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name”. Possess means own. We are going to own the remnant of Edom and all the nations. The heathen called by his name are those who call themselves Jews and Christians. Jew comes from Judah, which means praise of God, so Amalek is saying they are the praise of God, and they're not. Christian means anointed ones, calling themselves God's anointed. All of them that call themselves by those names, we are going to possess, “saith the Lord that doeth this”: he is going to make sure that thing is done.

precepts.text: The nation that will not serve Israel shall perish.
precepts.point: The residue of men seek after the Lord in servitude, and the Gentiles called by his name are those who call themselves Jews and Christians.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
Simeon's words, “That the residue of men might seek after the Lord”, can be confusing. How are they going to seek after the Lord? Isaiah answers it: “For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.”

They will seek after the Lord in captivity. There is no we're equal to you, we're ruling with you. The nations don't get a pass for all the evil they did. They are going to learn God's laws, his statutes and his commandments, and they will learn them in slavery, serving Israel. Whoever does not want to follow it shall be put to death. That is what the Bible says.

People online say the door is open for everyone, that God is going to take everybody in the same way. They don't understand. The residue of men seek the Lord by serving the kingdom of Israel, and the nation or kingdom that will not serve shall perish and be utterly wasted.

precepts.text: The nations that are left go up yearly to worship the King and keep the feast of tabernacles.
precepts.point: The residue of men seek after the Lord in servitude, and the Gentiles called by his name are those who call themselves Jews and Christians.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
Here is more on how the residue of men will seek after the Lord: “And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.”

What do they have to keep? The feast of tabernacles. The nations that are left will worship the King and keep the feast. When is the feast of tabernacles? The seventh month, the fifteenth day. So we are going to have to teach that to the nations: in the seventh month, on the fifteenth day, you go up towards Jerusalem to worship the King and you keep the feast of tabernacles.

That is what it means that the residue of men seek after the Lord. They come up under Israel, learning and keeping God's law, the law they would not keep before. It does not contradict Amos 9:12; it says the same thing. Amos just made it plain, while the way Simeon put it leaves people asking what it means.

precepts.text: The families that will not come up shall have no rain.
precepts.point: The residue of men seek after the Lord in servitude, and the Gentiles called by his name are those who call themselves Jews and Christians.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
There may be some rebellious heathen out there: “And it shall be, that whoso will not come up of all the families of the earth unto Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, even upon them shall be no rain.”

That is judgment. No rain means famine, no rain means dearth, no rain means death. Read on: “And if the family of Egypt go not up, and come not, that have no rain; there shall be the plague, wherewith the Lord will smite the heathen that come not up to keep the feast of tabernacles.”

So when Acts 15 says “That the residue of men might seek after the Lord, and all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called”, it is not an open door where everyone is equal. The residue of men will seek the Lord in servitude, keeping the feast, and those who refuse get no rain and the plague. And the Gentiles upon whom his name is called, those who call themselves Jews and Christians, God's praise and God's anointed: chains for them.

precepts.text: Paul said to Barnabas, Let us go again and visit our brethren in every city where we have preached the word of the Lord, and see how they do; the same circuit the leaders of old, like Samuel, kept every year.
precepts.point: That yearly circuit is leadership making its rounds, establishing the people and coming back to check on them, the same example Paul followed with the churches. These chapters close with the ark lost and regained, and Samuel rising up for the nation: prayer is a superpower, and that is how our mighty forefathers rolled, from Moses to Samuel to Judas Maccabeus all the way to Christ. Keep the commandments and send up that prayer, and the Most High will come down in thunder against your enemies.

note.label: 1 Samuel 7: Put Away the Strange Gods, and the Lord Thundered

precepts.why:
“Let us go again and visit our brethren in every city where we have preached the word of the Lord, and see how they do.” That is the same circuit the leaders of old kept.

Samuel “went from year to year in circuit to Beth–el, and Gilgal, and Mizpeh, and judged Israel in all those places. And his return was to Ramah; for there was his house.” Ramah was his headquarters. That yearly circuit is leadership making its rounds, establishing the people and coming back to check on them, the same example Paul followed with the churches.

These chapters close with the ark lost and regained, and Samuel rising up for the nation. Prayer is a superpower, and that is how our mighty forefathers rolled, from Moses to Samuel to Judas Maccabeus all the way to Christ.

precepts.text: To this agree the words of the prophets; David the prophet and Ezra the prophet say the same thing.
precepts.point: As far as the east is from the west, so far He removes our transgressions; He pities them that fear Him, for He knows we are dust.

note.label: Psalm 103: Bless the Lord for His Benefits to Israel

precepts.why:
“He hath not dealt with us after our sins; nor rewarded us according to our iniquities.” David the prophet says it, and he is not alone: “And to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written”.

To this agree the words of the prophets. David the prophet and Ezra the prophet say the same thing: the Most High has punished us less than our iniquities deserve. The prophets agree with one another, and the forgiveness of Israel's sins that David speaks of is what Christ came to do.

precepts.text: Even the New Testament points to future prophecy that He will return and build again the ruins of the tabernacle of David.
precepts.point: It shall be to Him a name of joy, a praise, and an honor before all nations, who will fear and tremble at the goodness He procures, for the nations know this is true and are struck when they see us carry ourselves as sons and daughters of the covenant.

note.label: Jeremiah 33: The Branch of Righteousness and the Covenant of Day and Night

precepts.why:
The New Testament reads the same prophecy as still ahead: “And to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written, After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down; and I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up”.

Even the New Testament points to future prophecy: he will return and build again the ruins of the tabernacle of David. That is the health and cure of Jeremiah 33, the captivity of Judah and Israel returned and built as at the first, cleansed from all their iniquity. The nations know this is true, and they are struck when they see us carry ourselves as sons and daughters of the covenant; they shall fear and tremble for all the goodness and prosperity he procures.

precepts.why:
“Simeon hath declared how God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name.”

That Simeon is Simon Peter. The same man is Simon, Simeon, Peter and Cephas. That is why the lists of the apostles read differently from book to book: the men are the same, known by different names.

precepts.point: As yet the Holy Ghost was fallen upon none of them; only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. They first had to believe in Christ in the place of animal sacrifice, believing that Christ could forgive sins when Moses' sacrifices could not. The subject matter of that day was the law and animal sacrifice versus the name of Jesus Christ, which is why the apostles keep saying to repent and believe in his name.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

precepts.why:
“But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.” These Pharisees were doing it after the name of Moses and animal sacrifice. But now it is under Christ and his name.

That is what being baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus meant in Samaria. The argument of that day was never the law itself; it was the law and animal sacrifice versus the name of Jesus Christ, and which name the forgiveness of sin comes under.

precepts.point: The doctrine back then was insisting on circumcision and keeping the law of Moses meaning animal sacrifice. Today the doctrines are different heresies but the same spirit.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
Paul marvels that the Israelites in Galatia were so soon removed from the gospel of Christ, from the teachings, unto another gospel “Which is not another.” We teach brothers and sisters and expect them to hold fast to what was taught, not to be persuaded otherwise. But Israelites that came out from among them were persuading and beguiling those Israelites in different regions of the diaspora.

Acts 15 confirms it: “certain which went out from us have troubled you with words, subverting your souls, saying, Ye must be circumcised, and keep the law: to whom we gave no such commandment.” Subverted means destroying, changing, altering. The doctrine back then was insisting on circumcision and keeping the law of Moses, meaning animal sacrifice. So the apostles sent chosen men “with our beloved Barnabas and Paul, Men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ”, and “Judas and Silas, who shall also tell you the same things by mouth.”

It is “not another” gospel because they use the same Bibles and the same scriptures, but with the wrong understanding; they bring the same scriptures but change the meaning. What happened then is happening now under a different name. Different doctrines come out, different names, but the same spirits doing the same things. Today the doctrines are different heresies but the same spirit.

precepts.point: There were always checks and balances. The leadership would steer you in the right direction.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Paul's second visit to Jerusalem, fourteen years after his first, is the history of Acts 15, and the majority of Paul's epistles and the issues he addresses extend around that chapter. “And certain men which came down from Judea taught the brethren, and said, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.” That meant getting circumcised to reestablish the covenant with Abraham and giving an animal sacrifice to reestablish the covenant of Moses.

“When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas, and certain other of them, should go up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question.” He went up by revelation, the spirit of the Lord leading him to Jerusalem. On the way “they passed through Phenice and Samaria, declaring the conversion of the Gentiles”, and when they came to Jerusalem “they were received of the church, and of the apostles and elders, and they declared all things that God had done with them.”

“privately to them which were of reputation” refers to the apostles and elders. “lest by any means I should run, or had run, in vain” means Paul had to check with the leadership to confirm he was on the right path. There were always checks and balances; the leadership would steer you in the right direction.

precepts.point: Paul warns in 1 Corinthians 9:27 that he keeps his body under subjection lest he himself become a castaway.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
The “false brethren unawares brought in” are identified in Acts 15: “But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.”

These were believers, of the sect of the Pharisees, who infiltrated the congregation with this doctrine. “was compelled to be circumcised” shows the Pharisees were going around forcefully telling people they had to be circumcised and return to animal sacrifice. Titus, being a Greek, brought up in Greek customs and fashion like Timothy whose father was a Greek, was an Israelite raised in Greek ways, not a Caucasian, and these false brethren wanted him circumcised to bring him into bondage.

precepts.point: Only through Christ could all 12 tribes receive salvation.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
After the dispute about circumcision and animal sacrifice, Peter switches to the topic of the Gentiles: “Men and brethren, ye know how that a good while ago God made choice among us, that the Gentiles by my mouth should hear the word of the gospel, and believe. And God, which knoweth the hearts, bare them witness, giving them the Holy Ghost, even as he did unto us; And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith.”

The reason he switches is this: if salvation required circumcision and animal sacrifice, the old covenant, then the northern kingdom, called Gentiles, strangers, heathens, could never receive salvation. So Peter asks, “Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?” That yoke is the bondage the false brethren were trying to bring the brethren into.

precepts.point: They are called brethren of the Gentiles. Romans 9:3-4 proves the apostles' brethren are Israelites.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

They are called brethren of the Gentiles. The heathen, the Gentiles and the uncircumcision that Paul went to are the brethren.

They were given a charge, with letters, “unto the brethren which are of the Gentiles in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia.” That is the fellowship Paul describes: the pillars sending him and Barnabas out with chief men of their own company, and Paul forward to do what they asked.
